close_reason: Resolved 2026-05-10: moved is_per_user_property from CalendarsBackend trait to jmap-calendars-types as the free fn is_per_user_calendar_event_property() plus const PER_USER_CALENDAR_EVENT_PROPERTIES. Eliminates the trait-method-with-default-impl divergence vector for the IANA-registered spec list. event.rs handler now calls the free fn directly. Added 4 unit tests pinning the list to the spec and exercising the classifier. README.md / PLAN.md trait sketches updated. cargo test --workspace clean; cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean. Commit b9b4469.
description:
src/backend.rs:119-124:

    fn is_per_user_property(prop: &str) -> bool {
        matches!(
            prop,
            "keywords" | "color" | "freeBusyStatus" | "useDefaultAlerts" | "alerts"
        )
    }

This is a method on the CalendarsBackend trait with a default impl that matches the spec list (draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.4 / §10.8.2). Two design issues:

1. It is a static fn (no &self / no Self::) so it could be a free function. As a trait method with default impl, a backend implementor could override it to return a different list — but the spec list is fixed by IANA registration. Allowing overrides invites silent divergence from the wire protocol.

2. It logically belongs to the protocol/types crate, not the server crate. jmap-calendars-types already owns the property registry (CalendarEventProperty enum at src/backend.rs lines 10-13 re-exports it). The per-user determination is metadata about a typed property, not about a backend.

Idiomatic fix:
- Move to jmap-calendars-types as either:
  (a) a const PER_USER_PROPERTIES: &[&str] = &["keywords", ...]; plus a free fn is_per_user_property(name: &str) -> bool
  (b) a method on the CalendarEventProperty enum: pub fn is_per_user(&self) -> bool { matches!(self, Self::Keywords | ...) }
- Drop the trait method here; have src/event.rs:233 call the free fn / enum method directly.

Option (b) is more idiomatic Rust — the property-level metadata travels with the property type. It also makes it impossible to misuse a stringly-typed name that doesn't appear in the registered enum.

Test gap: no unit test of is_per_user_property's correctness against the spec list. A simple table-driven test would catch a typo.

P3 — works correctly today. Idiom and architectural placement issue.
title: is_per_user_property on CalendarsBackend trait — hardcoded list, no &self, should be a free fn or in jmap-calendars-types
